# Overview



Welcome to the **Universal Biomedical Skills & Agents** platform — a Biomedical Operating System (BioOS) that transforms static scientific scripts into autonomous, agentic AI workflows. If you have ever wished that a single natural-language query could seamlessly route through 886 curated biomedical skills, execute across multiple LLM providers, and return validated results with safety checks, this is the project that makes it possible. This overview will orient you to the platform's purpose, its core architecture, and how the major components connect — giving you the conceptual map you need before diving into any specific subsystem.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L23-L28), [Skills/README.md](/Skills/README.md#L23-L27)

## What Is This Project?

At its heart, this repository is a **Biomedical Operating System** — a runtime platform that orchestrates a comprehensive library of skills, agents, and mathematical foundations for modern AI-driven life science research. Unlike traditional bioinformatics toolkits that require manual scripting for every pipeline step, this system transforms static scripts into **Agentic Workflows**: autonomous systems that plan, execute, use tools, and self-correct to solve complex scientific problems. The platform is designed to support high-impact research, clinical decision support, and automated laboratory operations — all accessible through a unified interface that works identically whether you are querying from a CLI, a REST API, or an MCP-compatible client like Claude Desktop.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L23-L28), [biokernel/README.md](/biokernel/README.md#L8-L22)

## The Big Picture: How It All Fits Together

Before examining individual components, it is essential to understand the data flow from the moment a user submits a biomedical query to the moment a validated response returns. The following diagram illustrates the core architecture:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["👤 User Query<br/>'Analyze JAK2 V617F in MPN patients'"] --> B

    subgraph B ["BioKernel Server (FastAPI)"]
        B1["Semantic Skill Router<br/>TF-IDF Cosine Similarity"]
        B2["DAG Workflow Engine<br/>Parallel Execution + Retry"]
        B3["Evaluation Engine<br/>Biomedical Assertions + LLM-as-Judge"]
        B1 --> B2 --> B3
    end

    B --> C["USDL Transpiler<br/>Write-Once, Deploy-Anywhere"]
    C --> D1["Anthropic Adapter<br/>XML + Thinking Tags"]
    C --> D2["OpenAI Adapter<br/>System Prompt + JSON Schema"]
    C --> D3["Gemini Adapter<br/>Role Cards + Constraints"]
    C --> D4["Local Adapter<br/>Ollama / llama3.1"]

    D1 & D2 & D3 & D4 --> E["Unified LLMResponse"]

    E --> F1["REST API (FastAPI)"]
    E --> F2["CLI (Rich Interactive)"]
    E --> F3["MCP Server (Claude Desktop)"]

    style A fill:#e1f5fe,stroke:#0277bd
    style B fill:#f3e5f5,stroke:#7b1fa2
    style C fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#ef6c00
    style E fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
```

The flow works as follows: a natural-language query enters the **BioKernel Server**, where the **Semantic Skill Router** matches it against 886 registered skills using TF-IDF cosine similarity (no GPU required). The matched skill is then either executed as a single agent call or orchestrated through the **DAG Workflow Engine** for multi-step pipelines. Before execution, the **USDL Transpiler** compiles the skill's canonical specification into a provider-optimized prompt bundle. The chosen **LLM Provider Adapter** (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, or local) executes the query, and the **Evaluation Engine** validates the response against biomedical assertions. Results are returned via REST API, CLI, or MCP protocol.

Sources: [biokernel/README.md](/biokernel/README.md#L31-L65), [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L74-L115)

## Core Architectural Components

The platform is built on four foundational pillars, each addressing a distinct challenge in biomedical AI orchestration:

| Component | Location | Purpose | Key Technology |
|-----------|----------|---------|----------------|
| **Semantic Skill Router** | `biokernel/biokernel/router.py` | Match natural-language queries to the best skill | TF-IDF + cosine similarity |
| **DAG Workflow Engine** | `biokernel/biokernel/workflow_engine.py` | Execute multi-step agent pipelines | Async topological execution |
| **USDL Transpiler** | `biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py` | Compile one skill spec into multi-provider formats | Provider-specific prompt compilation |
| **Evaluation Engine** | `biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py` | Validate outputs with biomedical assertions | Gene entity detection, safety checks, citation verification |

> [!TIP]
> The Semantic Skill Router runs in pure Python with no GPU dependency — it uses TF-IDF vectorization and cosine similarity with a default threshold of 0.35. This design choice ensures the platform can be deployed in resource-constrained environments while still providing substantially better routing than keyword matching alone.

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/router.py](/biokernel/biokernel/router.py#L1-L15), [biokernel/biokernel/workflow_engine.py](/biokernel/biokernel/workflow_engine.py#L1-L15), [biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py](/biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py#L1-L13), [biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py](/biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py#L1-L15)

## The Skills Ecosystem

The `Skills/` directory is the heart of the platform's knowledge — a curated collection of **886 biomedical AI skills** spanning 59+ domains. Each skill is defined using the **SKILL.md** standard, which makes capabilities discoverable, self-documenting, and executable by AI agents. Skills are organized into domain-specific directories:

| Domain | Directory | Featured Agents |
|--------|-----------|-----------------|
| **Genomics & Bioinformatics** | `Skills/Genomics/` | BioMaster (multi-pipeline orchestrator), CellAgent (single-cell QC), STAgent (spatial transcriptomics) |
| **Clinical & Operations** | `Skills/Clinical/` | ChatEHR (patient record assistant), TrialGPT (patient-to-trial matching), RadGPT (radiology reports) |
| **Drug Discovery & Chemistry** | `Skills/Drug_Discovery/` | MAGE (antibody design), CheMatAgent (computational chemistry), Medea (omics-driven discovery) |
| **Knowledge & Research** | `Skills/Research_Tools/` | KRAGEN (knowledge-graph RAG), LEADS (systematic review), Biomni (150+ tools) |
| **Agentic AI** | `Skills/Agentic_AI/` | DeepResearch Swarm, Claude Code Operations, Computer Use Agents |
| **MCP Servers** | `Skills/MCP_Servers/` | BioMCP (PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov), MCPmed (GEO, STRING) |

Every skill follows the same structural pattern — a `SKILL.md` definition file (required), an optional implementation script (`impl.py`), and an optional `references/` directory for supporting documentation. This uniformity is what enables the BioKernel to discover and route to any skill automatically.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L96-L106), [Skills/README.md](/Skills/README.md#L87-L97), [skills_catalog.json](/skills_catalog.json#L1-L6), [Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md](/Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md#L27-L35)

## The SKILL.md Standard

The **SKILL.md** standard is the lingua franca of this platform — the metadata format that makes every skill discoverable by the BioKernel router. A SKILL.md file combines YAML frontmatter for machine-readable metadata with Markdown body for operational instructions. The frontmatter captures the skill name, description, allowed tools, and compatibility constraints, while the body provides the workflow steps an agent should follow. When the BioKernel starts, it recursively scans all configured skill paths for `SKILL.md` files and `*_agent.py` scripts, parsing each into a `SkillMetadata` object that feeds the routing index. This design means adding a new capability to the platform is as simple as writing a correctly formatted SKILL.md file in the right directory.

```text
Skills/
└── Domain_Name/
    └── Skill_Name/
        ├── SKILL.md          # The Definition (Required)
        ├── impl.py           # The Implementation (Optional)
        └── references/       # Supporting docs (Optional)
```

Sources: [Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md](/Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md#L16-L35), [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L157-L197)

## Cross-Provider Abstraction: USDL

A central challenge in multi-LLM platforms is that each provider speaks a different prompt dialect — Anthropic expects XML-structured prompts with thinking blocks, OpenAI uses system/user messages with function schemas, and Gemini prefers role cards with structured context. The **Universal Skill Description Language (USDL)** solves this by providing a canonical, model-agnostic schema for defining biomedical skills. You write a skill spec once in USDL, and the transpiler compiles it into provider-specific artifacts:

| Provider | Compiled Artifact |
|----------|-------------------|
| **OpenAI** | System prompt + JSON schema bundle for ChatGPT Health / function calling |
| **Anthropic** | Claude coworker transcript template with `<thinking>/<analysis>/<decision>` XML tags |
| **Gemini** | Role card + output constraints tuned for long-context reasoning |

This "write-once, deploy-anywhere" approach ensures that a single skill definition stays in sync across all LLM backends — a critical property for maintaining auditability and safety compliance in clinical settings.

Sources: [docs/USDL_OVERVIEW.md](/docs/USDL_OVERVIEW.md#L14-L43), [biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py](/biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py#L132-L157)

## Execution Modes

The BioKernel supports three execution modes that cater to different usage patterns, from production APIs to exploratory research sessions:

| Mode | How It Works | Best For |
|------|-------------|----------|
| **Autonomous** | Automatic routing + execution — the system selects the best skill and runs it | Production APIs, batch processing, CI/CD pipelines |
| **Interactive** | User selects from ranked skill matches presented by the router | Exploratory research, learning the platform |
| **Manual** | User specifies an exact `skill_id` to bypass routing entirely | Debugging, benchmarking, targeted evaluation |

> [!TIP]
> When using Autonomous mode, the router's fallback chain tries Anthropic → OpenAI → Gemini → Local in sequence if your preferred provider is unavailable. Configure `default_provider` in `config.yaml` to set your preference, but always set at least one API key environment variable to avoid a "No LLM providers available" error.

Sources: [biokernel/README.md](/biokernel/README.md#L169-L178), [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L136-L153), [biokernel/config.yaml](/biokernel/config.yaml#L7-L33)

## Project Directory Map

Understanding where things live is the first step to working effectively with this codebase. Here is the top-level structure with the role of each major directory:

```text
.
├── Skills/                     # 886 biomedical AI skill definitions
│   ├── Genomics/               # Single-cell, spatial, CRISPR, variant interpretation
│   ├── Clinical/               # EHR, radiology, oncology, trial matching
│   ├── Drug_Discovery/         # Antibody design, chemistry, molecule design
│   ├── Agentic_AI/             # Orchestrators, swarms, planning agents
│   ├── MCP_Servers/            # Model Context Protocol servers (BioMCP, MCPmed)
│   ├── Research_Tools/         # Biomni, literature mining, knowledge graphs
│   └── TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md  # Guide for contributing new skills
│
├── biokernel/                  # BioKernel Runtime Platform (v2026.4.0)
│   ├── biokernel/              # Core: server, router, workflow engine, MCP server
│   ├── adapters/               # LLM provider adapters (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Local)
│   ├── interface/              # Abstract LLMProvider base class
│   ├── schema/                 # Pydantic type system (io_types.py)
│   ├── optimizer/              # USDL transpiler + meta-prompter
│   ├── evaluator/              # Assertion + LLM-judge evaluation engine
│   └── tests/                  # 74+ tests across all components
│
├── docs/                       # Documentation hub
│   ├── architecture/           # Repository maps + onboarding guides
│   ├── operations/             # Runbooks and stack documentation
│   ├── standards/              # USDL specification and governance
│   └── strategy/               # LLM curation playbook, platform strategy
│
├── tests/                      # Integration tests + scRNA-seq analysis scripts
├── skills_catalog.json         # Auto-generated catalog of all 886 skills
└── skills_reliability_report.json  # Skill reliability assessment data
```

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L95-L122), [biokernel/README.md](/biokernel/README.md#L192-L229)

## Configuration at a Glance

The platform is configured through `biokernel/config.yaml`, which controls provider selection, routing thresholds, workflow timeouts, and safety checks. Here are the key configuration knobs you should know about:

| Section | Key Setting | Default | What It Controls |
|---------|------------|---------|------------------|
| `default_provider` | — | `anthropic` | Which LLM provider to use when none is specified |
| `providers.*.model` | — | Varies | Model identifier per provider (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `gpt-4o`) |
| `routing.strategy` | — | `semantic` | Routing algorithm: `semantic`, `keyword`, or `hybrid` |
| `routing.similarity_threshold` | — | `0.35` | Minimum cosine similarity for a skill match |
| `workflow.retry_count` | — | `2` | Number of retries per failed workflow step |
| `evaluation.pass_threshold` | — | `0.80` | Minimum score for an evaluation case to pass |
| `evaluation.safety_pass_threshold` | — | `0.95` | Minimum safety score (stricter than general) |

Sources: [biokernel/config.yaml](/biokernel/config.yaml#L1-L76)

# Quick Start



Get from zero to your first biomedical AI query in under five minutes. This page walks you through installing the **BioKernel** platform, configuring your first LLM provider, executing a query, and exploring the 59+ biomedical skills — all without needing to understand the internal architecture.

## What You'll Need

Before starting, ensure your environment meets these prerequisites:

| Requirement | Minimum | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| **Python** | 3.11 | 3.12+ |
| **pip** | Latest stable | — |
| **LLM API Key** | At least one of: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or local Ollama | Anthropic (default) |
| **OS** | macOS / Linux | Ubuntu 22.04+ or macOS 14+ |
| **RAM** | 4 GB | 8 GB+ (for local models via Ollama) |

The BioKernel is a pure Python runtime — no GPU is required for the orchestration layer. A GPU is only needed if you plan to run local models through the Ollama adapter.

Sources: [biokernel/pyproject.toml](biokernel/pyproject.toml#L11-L12), [biokernel/README.md](biokernel/README.md#L13-L14)

## Installation

**Step 1 — Clone the repository:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mdbabumiamssm/LLMs-Universal-Life-Science-and-Clinical-Skills-.git
cd LLMs-Universal-Life-Science-and-Clinical-Skills-
```

**Step 2 — Install BioKernel with your preferred providers:**

```bash
cd biokernel

# Option A: All cloud providers (Anthropic + OpenAI + Gemini + Ollama)
pip install -e ".[all-providers]"

# Option B: Single provider only
pip install -e ".[anthropic]"      # Claude only
pip install -e ".[openai]"        # GPT only
pip install -e ".[google]"        # Gemini only
pip install -e ".[local]"         # Ollama only

# Option C: Full installation (all providers + biomedical libs + dev tools)
pip install -e ".[full]"
```

The table below shows what each optional dependency group pulls in:

| Group | Key Packages | When to Use |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `anthropic>=0.42.0` | Claude Sonnet/Opus as your LLM |
| `openai` | `openai>=1.58.0` | GPT-4o / GPT-4.1 as your LLM |
| `google` | `google-generativeai>=0.8.0` | Gemini 2.0 Flash as your LLM |
| `local` | `ollama>=0.4.0` | Self-hosted models (Llama 3.1, Mistral) |
| `eval` | `scikit-learn`, `scipy` | Running evaluation benchmarks |
| `bio` | `scanpy`, `anndata`, `biopython` | Single-cell / genomics analysis |
| `dev` | `pytest`, `ruff`, `mypy` | Contributing to the codebase |
| `full` | All of the above | Complete development environment |

> [!TIP]
> Use `pip install -e ".[all-providers]"` for the fastest path to a working system. You can always add `bio` or `eval` groups later.

Sources: [biokernel/pyproject.toml](biokernel/pyproject.toml#L34-L76), [biokernel/README.md](biokernel/README.md#L69-L75)

## Configure Your API Key

BioKernel reads provider credentials from **environment variables** — no keys are stored in config files. Set at least one API key before proceeding:

```bash
# Anthropic (default provider)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."

# OpenAI
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."

# Google Gemini
export GOOGLE_API_KEY="AIza..."

# Local (Ollama must be running on localhost:11434)
# No API key needed — just start Ollama separately
```

The `config.yaml` file maps each provider to its expected environment variable name. The default provider is `anthropic`, but you can override this per-query via the `--provider` flag.

| Config Key | Environment Variable | Default Model |
|---|---|---|
| `providers.anthropic.api_key_env` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` |
| `providers.openai.api_key_env` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `gpt-4o` |
| `providers.gemini.api_key_env` | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | `gemini-2.0-flash` |
| `providers.local.api_base` | (URL) | `llama3.1:8b` via Ollama |

> [!TIP]
> Verify your key is set: `echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY | head -c 10` should print the first characters without errors. If you see a blank line, the variable is unset.

Sources: [biokernel/config.yaml](biokernel/config.yaml#L9-L33), [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L119-L134)

## Your First Query

With installation and API keys in place, you have **three execution modes** to choose from. Here's how each one works:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[You have a biomedical query] --> B{How do you want to run it?}
    B --> C[CLI: Single Command]
    B --> D[CLI: Interactive Session]
    B --> E[API: HTTP Server]
    
    C --> F["biokernel run 'your query'"]
    F --> G[Auto-route → Execute → Print result]
    
    D --> H["biokernel interactive"]
    H --> I[Chat loop with skill discovery]
    
    E --> J["biokernel serve --port 8000"]
    J --> K[POST /v1/agent/run]
    K --> L[JSON response with skill metadata]
```

### Mode 1 — Single-Command Execution (Fastest)

```bash
cd biokernel

# Autonomous: BioKernel picks the best skill automatically
biokernel run "Analyze JAK2 V617F mutation in MPN patients" --provider anthropic

# Manual: Force a specific skill by ID
biokernel run "Analyze JAK2 V617F mutation in MPN patients" --provider openai --skill variant-interpretation
```

The CLI renders a rich panel showing the matched skill name, LLM provider/model used, and execution time. If safety flags are triggered (e.g., clinical content without disclaimer), they appear as warnings below the result.

### Mode 2 — Interactive Research Session

```bash
biokernel interactive --provider anthropic
```

This opens a chat loop with built-in commands:

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `skills` | List all 59+ registered skills |
| `providers` | Show which LLM providers are currently available |
| `help` | Print available commands |
| `quit` / `exit` | End the session |
| *any other text* | Routed as a biomedical query |

### Mode 3 — API Server (For Integration)

```bash
# Start the server
biokernel serve --port 8000

# In another terminal, execute a query via curl
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/agent/run \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "What are the ACMG criteria for BRCA1 c.68_69del?"}'
```

The server exposes these REST endpoints:

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/` | Health check + system status |
| `POST` | `/v1/agent/run` | Execute a biomedical query |
| `POST` | `/v1/workflow/run` | Execute a multi-step DAG workflow |
| `GET` | `/v1/skills` | List all registered skills |
| `GET` | `/v1/providers` | List available LLM providers |
| `POST` | `/v1/route` | Preview routing without execution |

Sources: [biokernel/README.md](biokernel/README.md#L79-L132), [biokernel/cli.py](biokernel/cli.py#L84-L246), [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L74-L115)

## Explore the Skills Catalog

BioKernel ships with **59+ biomedical skill domains** spanning genomics, clinical decision support, drug discovery, and more. To see what's available:

```bash
# List all registered skills (rich table format)
biokernel skills

# Filter by category
biokernel skills --category genomics
biokernel skills --category clinical
```

The skill catalog is organized into domain directories under `Skills/`. Here's a map of the primary domains and representative agents:

```
Skills/
├── Genomics/                  # 🧬 BioMaster, CellAgent, STAgent, CRISPR agents
├── Clinical/                  # 🏥 ChatEHR, TrialGPT, RadGPT, Oncology agents
├── Drug_Discovery/            # 🧪 MAGE, CheMatAgent, Medea
├── Research_Tools/            # 🔍 Biomni, KRAGEN, LEADS
├── MCP_Servers/               # 🔌 BioMCP, MCPmed
├── Agentic_AI/                # 🤖 Claude Code Ops, Computer Use Agents
├── AI_Providers/              # ☁️ OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, AWS, Azure skills
├── Pathology_AI/              # 🔬 H&E analysis, digital pathology
├── Oncology/                  # 🎯 Precision oncology, tumor boards
├── Protein_Science/           # 🧫 Structure prediction, design
├── Multi_Omics/               # 📊 Integration, multi-modal analysis
├── Spatial_Omics/             # 🗺️ Visium/Xenium, spatial analysis
├── ... (40+ more domains)
```

Each skill follows the **SKILL.md** standard — a YAML frontmatter + Markdown body format that makes skills discoverable by the semantic router. You can directly invoke any skill that has a Python implementation:

```bash
# Match a patient to a clinical trial
python3 Skills/Clinical/Trial_Matching/TrialGPT/run_matching.py \
    --patient_profile ./patient.json

# Design an antibody
python3 Skills/Drug_Discovery/Antibody_Design/MAGE/generate.py \
    --antigen "spike_protein" --count 5

# Analyze spatial transcriptomics
python3 Skills/Genomics/Spatial_Transcriptomics/STAgent/main.py \
    --data ./visium_data.h5ad --task "cluster_domains"
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L95-L122), [Skills/README.md](Skills/README.md#L87-L122), [biokernel/skills_catalog.py](biokernel/skills_catalog.py#L73-L98)

## Connect to Claude Desktop via MCP

BioKernel includes a **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server that exposes all skills as tools to MCP-compatible clients like Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Cursor. This is the easiest way to use biomedical skills inside your existing AI workflow.

**Step 1 — Start the MCP server:**

```bash
biokernel mcp
```

**Step 2 — Configure your MCP client** (e.g., Claude Desktop `claude_desktop_config.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "biokernel": {
      "command": "biokernel",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

The MCP server exposes four tools to connected clients:

| MCP Tool | What It Does |
|---|---|
| `run_bio_agent` | Execute any registered biomedical skill via natural language |
| `list_skills` | Discover available skills with descriptions and categories |
| `route_query` | Preview which skills match a query (no execution) |
| `run_workflow` | Execute a multi-step DAG workflow (e.g., literature → design → safety) |

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/mcp_server.py](biokernel/biokernel/mcp_server.py#L44-L138), [biokernel/README.md](biokernel/README.md#L97-L101), [Skills/MCP_Servers/BioMCP/SKILL.md](Skills/MCP_Servers/BioMCP/SKILL.md#L36-L54)

## Run Evaluations

BioKernel includes a **biomedical evaluation framework** with domain-specific assertions (gene entity detection, safety disclaimer validation, citation checking) and LLM-as-judge rubrics. To validate skill performance:

```bash
# Run evaluation suite
biokernel eval tests/eval_cases.yaml --html

# Run with pytest (unit/integration tests)
pytest biokernel/tests/ -v

# Run with coverage report
pytest biokernel/tests/ --cov=biokernel --cov-report=html
```

The evaluation engine checks skills against a configurable pass threshold (default 0.80) and a stricter safety threshold (0.95). HTML reports are generated per provider for cross-platform comparison.

| Setting | Default | Config Key |
|---|---|---|
| Pass threshold | 0.80 | `evaluation.pass_threshold` |
| Safety pass threshold | 0.95 | `evaluation.safety_pass_threshold` |
| Max evaluation time | 120s | `evaluation.max_eval_time_seconds` |
| Reports directory | `./reports` | `evaluation.reports_dir` |

Sources: [biokernel/config.yaml](biokernel/config.yaml#L63-L68), [biokernel/README.md](biokernel/README.md#L109-L113), [biokernel/cli.py](biokernel/cli.py#L171-L193)

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `No LLM providers available` | No API key set | Export the matching env var (e.g., `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...`) |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: biokernel` | Not installed or wrong directory | Run `pip install -e ".[all-providers]"` from the `biokernel/` directory |
| `Root directory not found: Skills` | Running from wrong working directory | Ensure `Skills/` is a sibling of `biokernel/` in your CWD |
| Rich output not rendering | `rich` not installed | Install with `pip install rich>=13.9.0` |
| MCP client can't connect | Server not in PATH | Ensure `biokernel` CLI is on your system PATH after install |
| Provider fallback triggered | Requested provider unavailable | Check API key validity; BioKernel falls back through `anthropic → openai → gemini → local` |

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L136-L153), [biokernel/skills_catalog.py](biokernel/skills_catalog.py#L88-L91), [biokernel/cli.py](biokernel/cli.py#L32-L46)

| Your Goal | Next Page |

# SKILL.md Standard



The **SKILL.md Standard** is the self-documenting contract that makes every AI capability in this repository discoverable, executable, and safe. Think of it as a résumé for each skill — a machine-readable file that tells the BioKernel engine *what the skill does, when to trigger it, how to run it, and what guardrails apply*. With **886 skills** already indexed across the repository, this standard is the single reason an autonomous agent can navigate the entire biomedical skills library without human guidance. This page explains the format from the ground up, walks through real examples, and shows you how the BioKernel validates your SKILL.md at scan time.

Sources: [skills_catalog.json](skills_catalog.json#L1-L10), [Skills/README.md](Skills/README.md#L84-L95)

## Why a Standard Matters

Without a standard, every skill is an island — a folder of scripts with no consistent entry point. An AI agent (or a developer) must open files, guess what they do, and hope the code matches the README. The SKILL.md Standard solves three core problems at once:

| Problem | What SKILL.md Provides |
|---|---|
| **Discoverability** — "Which skill handles X?" | The `name`, `description`, and `keywords` fields act as a semantic index. The BioKernel scanner reads every SKILL.md and builds a searchable catalog. |
| **Executability** — "How do I run it?" | The `allowed-tools`, `compatibility`, and `Workflow` sections tell the agent exactly which tools to invoke and in what order. |
| **Safety** — "What can go wrong?" | The `allowed-tools` whitelist sandboxes each skill, and the `measurable_outcome` field sets a verifiable success criterion. |

The result is a **Biomedical Operating System** where skills are not just files on disk — they are first-class, addressable capabilities that any LLM can discover, reason about, and invoke programmatically.

Sources: [Skills/README.md](Skills/README.md#L30-L38), [Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md](Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md#L14-L20)

## Anatomy of a SKILL.md File

Every SKILL.md is composed of two parts: a **YAML frontmatter block** enclosed in `---` delimiters, and a **Markdown body** that documents the skill in human-readable form. The frontmatter is the machine-parseable contract; the body is the operational guide for the agent. Here is a visual overview of how these parts relate:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["SKILL.md File"] --> B["YAML Frontmatter<br/>(Machine-Readable)"]
    A --> C["Markdown Body<br/>(Agent-Operable Guide)"]
    B --> D["Identity: name, description, keywords"]
    B --> E["Constraints: allowed-tools, measurable_outcome, compatibility"]
    B --> F["Provenance: metadata, license, reliability"]
    C --> G["When to Use This Skill"]
    C --> H["Core Capabilities"]
    C --> I["Workflow Steps"]
    C --> J["Example Usage"]
    C --> K["Guardrails / References"]
```

Sources: [Skills/Genomics/CRISPR_Design_Agent/SKILL.md](Skills/Genomics/CRISPR_Design_Agent/SKILL.md#L14-L26), [Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md](Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md#L32-L56)

## Directory Structure Convention

Each skill lives in its own folder under a domain category. The SKILL.md file is the **required** entry point; implementation files and reference materials are optional.

```text
Skills/
└── Domain_Name/                # e.g., Clinical, Genomics, Drug_Discovery
    └── Skill_Name/             # e.g., CRISPR_Design_Agent, ChatEHR
        ├── SKILL.md            # ✅ Required — The skill definition
        ├── impl.py             # ⬜ Optional — Python implementation
        ├── agent.py            # ⬜ Optional — Agent entry point
        ├── references/         # ⬜ Optional — Supporting docs
        │   └── rules.md
        └── requirements.txt    # ⬜ Optional — Dependencies
```

The BioKernel scanner recursively searches for any file named `SKILL.md` under the `Skills/` root, so the exact nesting depth does not matter — only that the file exists and is well-formed.

Sources: [Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md](Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md#L27-L35), [biokernel/skills_catalog.py](biokernel/skills_catalog.py#L69-L72)

## YAML Frontmatter Reference

The frontmatter is parsed by the BioKernel's `skills_catalog.py` using **PyYAML** — not homebrew string parsing — so you can use standard YAML syntax including multi-line strings and nested objects. The scanner enforces two **required fields** and logs errors for any skill that omits them.

### Required Fields

| Field | Type | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Unique skill identifier (kebab-case) | `crispr-guide-design` |
| `description` | string | One-sentence summary; acts as the "prompt" for skill selection | `Guide foundry for CRISPR sgRNA design` |

> [!TIP]
> The `description` field is the most important line you will write. It is what the BioKernel's Semantic Skill Router uses to match a user's intent to your skill. Write it as if you are explaining the skill to an AI that has never seen it before — be specific, include key nouns, and state the outcome.

### Recommended Fields

| Field | Type | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keywords` | list of strings | Core terms for indexing and search | `[CRISPR, sgRNA, off-target]` |
| `measurable_outcome` | string | SMART goal defining success | `Return ≥4 guides with scores within 10 min` |
| `allowed-tools` | list of strings | Security sandbox — tools the agent may use | `[run_shell_command, read_file]` |
| `tool_type` | string | Execution mode hint | `python`, `cli`, or `mixed` |
| `primary_tool` | string | Main library or binary the skill depends on | `cooltools`, `requests` |
| `license` | string | Open-source license | `MIT`, `Apache-2.0` |
| `compatibility` | list of objects | Runtime requirements | `[{system: Python 3.10+}]` |
| `metadata` | object | Author, version, and provenance | See below |

### Metadata Sub-Object

The `metadata` field carries provenance information:

```yaml
metadata:
  author: CRISPR-GPT Team
  version: "1.0.0"
```

### Reliability Sub-Object

Some skills include a `reliability` block that scores upstream data sources. The BioKernel extracts these into a separate reliability report during catalog generation:

```yaml
reliability:
  - source: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy
    score: 0.90
    rationale: >
      Scanpy repository maintained by the scverse core team with
      actively tested QC utilities.
```

Sources: [biokernel/skills_catalog.py](biokernel/skills_catalog.py#L44-L67), [Skills/Genomics/CRISPR_Design_Agent/SKILL.md](Skills/Genomics/CRISPR_Design_Agent/SKILL.md#L14-L26), [Skills/Genomics/Single_Cell_RNA_QC/SKILL.md](Skills/Genomics/Single_Cell_RNA_QC/SKILL.md#L11-L22)

## Markdown Body Structure

The body section is what an AI agent reads *after* it has selected your skill. It must answer three questions in order: **When should I use this?**, **What can it do?**, and **How do I run it?** The following table shows the recommended sections and their purpose:

| Section | Purpose | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| `# Skill Title` | Re-states the skill name with a one-paragraph overview | ✅ Yes |
| `## When to Use This Skill` | Trigger conditions — when should the agent select this skill? | ✅ Yes |
| `## Core Capabilities` | Numbered list of what the skill can accomplish | ✅ Yes |
| `## Workflow` | Ordered step-by-step procedure the agent should follow | ✅ Yes |
| `## Example Usage` | Concrete user prompt + agent action (CLI command or API call) | ✅ Yes |
| `## Guardrails` | Safety constraints, assumptions, and boundary conditions | ⬜ Recommended |
| `## References` | Links to related skills, papers, or internal docs | ⬜ Recommended |
| `## Related Skills` | Cross-references to other SKILL.md files | ⬜ Recommended |

Sources: [Skills/Genomics/CRISPR_Design_Agent/SKILL.md](Skills/Genomics/CRISPR_Design_Agent/SKILL.md#L28-L72), [Skills/Clinical/Oncology/Autonomous_Oncology_Agent/SKILL.md](Skills/Clinical/Oncology/Autonomous_Oncology_Agent/SKILL.md#L29-L77)

## Real-World Examples

The repository contains 886 skills spanning domains from 3D Genomics to Software Engineering. Here are three representative examples that illustrate the range of the standard.

### Example 1: Knowledge-Heavy Skill (ClinVar Lookup)

This skill wraps REST API and local VCF queries for clinical variant interpretation. Notice how the body includes **code snippets** inside the workflow — the agent can copy-paste these directly:

```yaml
---
name: bio-clinical-databases-clinvar-lookup
description: Query ClinVar for variant pathogenicity classifications,
  review status, and disease associations via REST API or local VCF.
tool_type: python
primary_tool: requests
measurable_outcome: Execute skill workflow successfully with valid
  output within 15 minutes.
allowed-tools:
  - read_file
  - run_shell_command
---
```

The body includes reference tables (clinical significance categories, review status stars), batch annotation commands, and cross-references to related skills like `variant-prioritization`.

Sources: [Skills/Clinical/Clinical_Databases/clinvar-lookup/SKILL.md](Skills/Clinical/Clinical_Databases/clinvar-lookup/SKILL.md#L12-L22)

### Example 2: Multimodal Agent (Autonomous Oncology)

This skill combines vision models and LLM reasoning — a more complex pattern where the `allowed-tools` whitelist is critical for safety:

```yaml
---
name: autonomous-oncology-agent
description: Precision Oncology
keywords:
  - oncology
  - multimodal
  - H&E
  - biomarkers
  - NCCN
measurable_outcome: Generate a prioritized treatment plan with evidence
  levels and predicted biomarker status within 5 minutes of data ingest.
allowed-tools:
  - run_shell_command
  - web_fetch
---
```

The `measurable_outcome` is specific and time-bound — the agent and its evaluators can verify success objectively.

Sources: [Skills/Clinical/Oncology/Autonomous_Oncology_Agent/SKILL.md](Skills/Clinical/Oncology/Autonomous_Oncology_Agent/SKILL.md#L14-L26)

### Example 3: QC Pipeline with Reliability Scores (scRNA-seq QC)

This skill demonstrates the `reliability` field, which the catalog scanner extracts into a separate report:

```yaml
---
name: scrna-qc
description: Execute the MAD-based single-cell RNA-seq QC workflow
  to filter low-quality cells and emit reports plus filtered AnnData files.
measurable_outcome: Produce filtered .h5ad files, before/after plots,
  and qc_summary.json within 20 minutes per dataset.
reliability:
  - source: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy
    score: 0.90
    rationale: >
      Scanpy repository maintained by the scverse core team with
      actively tested QC utilities.
---
```

Sources: [Skills/Genomics/Single_Cell_RNA_QC/SKILL.md](Skills/Genomics/Single_Cell_RNA_QC/SKILL.md#L11-L22)

## How the BioKernel Discovers and Validates Skills

The BioKernel's catalog scanner (`biokernel/skills_catalog.py`) is the runtime enforcement mechanism for the SKILL.md Standard. Understanding its pipeline helps you write SKILL.md files that pass validation on the first attempt.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Scan Skills/ directory<br/>recursively for SKILL.md"] --> B["Strip HTML comment<br/>headers from content"]
    B --> C["Parse YAML frontmatter<br/>via PyYAML safe_load"]
    C --> D{"Frontmatter<br/>found?"}
    D -- No --> E["⚠️ Warning:<br/>Missing frontmatter"]
    D -- Yes --> F{"Required fields<br/>present?"}
    F -- No --> G["❌ Error:<br/>Missing name/description"]
    F -- Yes --> H["Enrich with file metadata<br/>(path, last_modified, body_length)"]
    H --> I["Extract capabilities<br/>from body headings"]
    I --> J["Extract reliability scores<br/>if present"]
    J --> K["Append to catalog list"]
    K --> L["Write skills_catalog.json<br/>+ skills_reliability_report.json"]
```

The scanner performs these validation steps in order:

1. **Comment stripping**: Removes any HTML comment banners (`<!-- ... -->`) before the `---` delimiter so frontmatter is parseable. This is necessary because many skills include a copyright notice as an HTML comment at the top of the file.
2. **YAML parsing**: Uses `yaml.safe_load()` on the text between the `---` delimiters. If parsing fails, a warning is logged and the skill is skipped.
3. **Required field check**: Verifies that both `name` and `description` exist. Missing fields are recorded as errors in the catalog output.
4. **Reliability extraction**: If a `reliability` or `source_reliability` block exists, each entry must be a dictionary with `source` (string) and `score` (numeric) keys. Malformed entries produce errors.
5. **Output generation**: Writes `skills_catalog.json` (full catalog) and `skills_reliability_report.json` (reliability scores only).

> [!TIP]
> Always place any HTML copyright comments **before** the opening `---` delimiter, never inside the frontmatter block. The scanner strips leading comments automatically, but comments embedded between the two `---` markers will cause a YAML parse error and your skill will be silently skipped from the catalog.

Sources: [biokernel/skills_catalog.py](biokernel/skills_catalog.py#L43-L83), [biokernel/skills_catalog.py](biokernel/skills_catalog.py#L88-L155)

## SKILL.md and USDL: Two Layers of the Same Architecture

The SKILL.md Standard and the **Universal Skill Definition Language (USDL)** serve complementary roles in this repository. SKILL.md is the *authoring format* — a Markdown file that a human writes in a skill folder. USDL is the *interchange format* — a JSON schema that the BioKernel transpiles into provider-specific artifacts (OpenAI system prompts, Anthropic coworker templates, Gemini role cards).

| Aspect | SKILL.md | USDL (JSON) |
|---|---|---|
| **Audience** | Developers writing skills | BioKernel transpiler generating provider payloads |
| **Location** | Inside each skill folder | Generated or authored separately |
| **Scope** | Single skill definition | Cross-provider deployment spec with `platform_configs` |
| **Safety** | `allowed-tools` whitelist | `validation.test_cases` + `safety` policies |
| **Execution** | Agent reads workflow steps | Transpiler emits system prompts + function schemas |

The flow from authoring to deployment is: **Write SKILL.md → BioKernel scans into catalog → USDL spec authored or derived → USDLTranspiler compiles to provider artifacts → Skill runs on any LLM**.

Sources: [docs/standards/USDL_OVERVIEW.md](docs/standards/USDL_OVERVIEW.md#L6-L29), [biokernel/schema/usdl_schema_v1.json](biokernel/schema/usdl_schema_v1.json#L1-L30)

## Complete Template

Here is the full SKILL.md template incorporating all the patterns observed across the repository's 886 skills:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill-name
description: A one-sentence description of what this skill does.
keywords:
  - keyword1
  - keyword2
tool_type: python
primary_tool: library_name
measurable_outcome: Specific, time-bound success criterion.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Your Name
  version: "1.0.0"
compatibility:
  - system: Python 3.10+
allowed-tools:
  - read_file
  - run_shell_command
reliability:
  - source: https://github.com/example/upstream
    score: 0.85
    rationale: >
      Brief justification for the reliability score.
---

# My Skill Name

A more detailed description of the skill.

## When to Use This Skill

*   Trigger condition 1
*   Trigger condition 2

## Core Capabilities

1.  **Capability A**: Description.
2.  **Capability B**: Description.

## Workflow

1.  **Step 1**: What the agent should do first.
2.  **Step 2**: The command to run or file to read.
3.  **Step 3**: How to interpret and present the output.

## Example Usage

**User**: "Do X."

**Agent Action**:
```bash
python3 Skills/Domain/MySkill/impl.py --arg "value"
```

## Guardrails

-   State assumptions (e.g., genome build, Cas variant).
-   Define boundary conditions (e.g., "QC only — doublet handling is separate").
-   Flag anything requiring manual review.

## Related Skills

-   other-skill-name - Brief description of relationship
```

Sources: [Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md](Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md#L38-L76), [Skills/Genomics/CRISPR_Design_Agent/SKILL.md](Skills/Genomics/CRISPR_Design_Agent/SKILL.md#L14-L72)

## Best Practices

The following principles emerge from the patterns observed across the repository's skill library:

| Principle | What It Means | Anti-Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| **Atomic** | One skill does one thing well | A single skill that does both QC *and* batch correction |
| **Discoverable** | Clear `name`, specific `description`, relevant `keywords` | Vague descriptions like "Helps with genomics" |
| **Safe** | `allowed-tools` whitelist limits scope; guardrails section states boundaries | Granting `web_fetch` to a skill that only needs `read_file` |
| **Contextual** | `references/` folder for complex rules; `reliability` for upstream trust scores | Embedding 500 lines of policy text in the body |
| **Measurable** | `measurable_outcome` is specific and time-bound | "Works correctly" with no success criterion |
| **Consistent** | Follow the section ordering: When → Capabilities → Workflow → Example → Guardrails | Scattered workflow steps mixed with capabilities |

Sources: [Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md](Skills/TUTORIAL_ADDING_NEW_SKILLS.md#L78-L83), [Skills/Genomics/Single_Cell_RNA_QC/SKILL.md](Skills/Genomics/Single_Cell_RNA_QC/SKILL.md#L31-L41)

Now that you understand the SKILL.md Standard, the logical next steps are:

- **See it in action**: Read [Architecture Overview](4-architecture-overview) to understand how the BioKernel uses the catalog at runtime to route user requests to the right skill.
- **Start building**: Follow [Adding New Skills](17-adding-new-skills) for a step-by-step walkthrough of creating your first SKILL.md and registering it in the catalog.
- **Go deeper on transpilation**: Read [USDL Transpiler](8-usdl-transpiler) to learn how SKILL.md definitions are compiled into provider-specific artifacts for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini.

# Architecture Overview



The Universal Biomedical Skills Platform operates as a **Biomedical Operating System (BioOS)** — a layered orchestration engine that transforms 59+ static biomedical skill domains into autonomous, agentic workflows. At its core lies **BioKernel**, a FastAPI runtime that discovers skills from the filesystem, routes natural-language queries to the best-matching skill via lightweight semantic similarity, and executes them through a provider-agnostic abstraction layer. The architectural design follows a single governing principle: **write a skill once in USDL (Universal Skill Description Language), deploy it optimally across Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and local LLM backends**. This page maps the complete system topology — from user request to LLM response — establishing the structural foundation that subsequent deep-dive pages will expand upon.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L200), [biokernel/README.md](/biokernel/README.md#L1-L200)

## System Architecture Diagram

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end request flow through the BioKernel platform. Each colored region represents a distinct architectural concern: **routing** (how queries find their skill), **execution** (how skills become LLM prompts), **abstraction** (how one skill runs on any provider), and **interface** (how external systems connect).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Interfaces
        CLI["CLI<br/>(click + Rich)"]
        REST["REST API<br/>(FastAPI :8000)"]
        MCP["MCP Server<br/>(JSON-RPC stdio)"]
    end

    subgraph BioKernel Core
        BK["BioKernel<br/>Orchestrator"]
        SR["Semantic Skill Router<br/>(TF-IDF + Cosine)"]
        WE["DAG Workflow Engine<br/>(Parallel + Retry)"]
        SC["Safety Checker"]
    end

    subgraph Cross-Provider Layer
        UT["USDL Transpiler"]
        LF["LLM Factory<br/>(Registry + Cache)"]
    end

    subgraph Provider Adapters
        AA["Anthropic Adapter<br/>(Claude XML)"]
        OA["OpenAI Adapter<br/>(Function Schemas)"]
        GA["Gemini Adapter<br/>(Role Cards)"]
        LA["Local Adapter<br/>(Ollama)"]
    end

    subgraph Skill Discovery
        SM["SKILL.md Scanner"]
        PA["Python Agent Scanner"]
        CAT["Skills Catalog<br/>(skills_catalog.json)"]
    end

    subgraph Evaluation
        EE["Evaluation Engine"]
        AC["Assertion Checker"]
        LJ["LLM-as-Judge"]
    end

    CLI --> BK
    REST --> BK
    MCP --> BK

    BK --> SR
    BK --> WE
    BK --> SC

    BK --> UT
    BK --> LF

    LF --> AA
    LF --> OA
    LF --> GA
    LF --> LA

    BK --> SM
    BK --> PA
    SM --> CAT
    PA --> CAT

    BK --> EE
    EE --> AC
    EE --> LJ

    SR -->|routes query to| CAT
    UT -->|compiles for| AA
    UT -->|compiles for| OA
    UT -->|compiles for| GA
```

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L1-L200), [biokernel/biokernel/router.py](/biokernel/biokernel/router.py#L1-L187), [biokernel/biokernel/workflow_engine.py](/biokernel/biokernel/workflow_engine.py#L1-L200)

## Core Execution Pipeline

Every user query passes through a **four-stage pipeline** within the BioKernel orchestrator: **Route → Compile → Execute → Safeguard**. The `BioKernel` class in `server.py` is the central coordinator — it is independent of FastAPI and can be used programmatically in scripts, notebooks, or embedded applications. The FastAPI application wraps this core with REST endpoints, lifecycle management, and CORS middleware.

**Stage 1 — Routing**: The `SkillRouter` receives the natural-language query and computes TF-IDF cosine similarity against all registered skill metadata (name, description, tags, capabilities, category). Skills exceeding the configurable `similarity_threshold` (default 0.35) are ranked and the top match is selected. If the user specifies an explicit `skill_id`, the router short-circuits to an exact match with score 1.0. This lightweight approach avoids GPU-hosted embedding models while delivering substantially better routing than keyword matching alone.

**Stage 2 — Compilation**: The selected skill's `SkillMetadata` — including its `instructions_body` (the full markdown content from SKILL.md) and `safety_checks` — is woven into a context-aware system prompt. The `_build_system_prompt` method constructs a base biomedical persona with mandatory safety disclaimers, then appends skill-specific instructions. If the skill was defined via USDL, the `USDLTranspiler` further compiles it into provider-optimized payloads: XML-structured prompts with thinking blocks for Anthropic, system/user messages with function schemas for OpenAI, and role cards with structured context for Gemini.

**Stage 3 — Execution**: The `LLMFactory` resolves the requested provider (with a fallback chain: anthropic → openai → gemini → local) and dispatches the standardized `LLMRequest`. Each adapter implements the `LLMProvider` abstract interface, normalizing provider-specific APIs into unified `LLMResponse` objects containing text, tool calls, usage metrics, and latency. For multi-step workflows, the `WorkflowEngine` executes DAGs with automatic parallelization of independent steps, configurable retry with exponential backoff, and step-level timeout enforcement.

**Stage 4 — Safeguarding**: The `_check_safety` method scans generated output for dangerous content patterns (`synthesize`, `self-medicate`, `without prescription`) and validates that clinical content includes appropriate disclaimers. Safety flags are attached to the `AgentResponse` and surfaced to the caller.

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L200-L399), [biokernel/biokernel/router.py](/biokernel/biokernel/router.py#L68-L130), [biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py](/biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py#L1-L200), [biokernel/interface/llm_provider.py](/biokernel/interface/llm_provider.py#L1-L121)

## Layer-by-Layer Component Map

The platform is organized into six architectural layers, each with a clear contract boundary. The table below maps every major component to its layer, responsibility, and primary source file.

| Layer | Component | Responsibility | Source |
|-------|-----------|----------------|--------|
| **Interface** | FastAPI Server | REST endpoints, lifecycle, CORS | [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L399-L547) |
| **Interface** | CLI (`biokernel` command) | Interactive + batch execution, Rich TUI | [biokernel/cli.py](/biokernel/cli.py#L1-L200) |
| **Interface** | MCP Server | JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio for Claude Desktop/Code | [biokernel/biokernel/mcp_server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/mcp_server.py#L1-L200) |
| **Orchestration** | BioKernel Core | Pipeline coordination: route → compile → execute → safeguard | [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L55-L199) |
| **Orchestration** | SkillRouter | TF-IDF semantic matching with cosine similarity | [biokernel/biokernel/router.py](/biokernel/biokernel/router.py#L38-L187) |
| **Orchestration** | WorkflowEngine | DAG execution, parallel steps, retry + timeout | [biokernel/biokernel/workflow_engine.py](/biokernel/biokernel/workflow_engine.py#L1-L277) |
| **Abstraction** | USDL Transpiler | Canonical spec → provider-specific prompt + schema bundles | [biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py](/biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py#L1-L326) |
| **Abstraction** | LLMFactory | Dynamic provider registry, creation, and caching | [biokernel/adapters/factory.py](/biokernel/adapters/factory.py#L1-L119) |
| **Abstraction** | LLMProvider (ABC) | Unified interface: `generate`, `generate_with_tools`, `stream` | [biokernel/interface/llm_provider.py](/biokernel/interface/llm_provider.py#L1-L121) |
| **Provider** | AnthropicAdapter | Claude API with XML prompts + tool definitions | [biokernel/adapters/anthropic_adapter.py](/biokernel/adapters/anthropic_adapter.py) |
| **Provider** | OpenAIRuntimeAdapter | GPT API with function schemas | [biokernel/adapters/openai_runtime_adapter.py](/biokernel/adapters/openai_runtime_adapter.py) |
| **Provider** | GeminiAdapter | Gemini API with role cards | [biokernel/adapters/gemini_adapter.py](/biokernel/adapters/gemini_adapter.py) |
| **Provider** | LocalAdapter | Ollama / local model inference | [biokernel/adapters/local_adapter.py](/biokernel/adapters/local_adapter.py) |
| **Discovery** | SKILL.md Scanner | YAML frontmatter + markdown body parsing | [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L162-L230) |
| **Discovery** | Python Agent Scanner | `*_agent.py` file detection and registration | [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L143-L160) |
| **Discovery** | Skills Catalog Generator | Recursive scan, validation, JSON catalog output | [biokernel/skills_catalog.py](/biokernel/skills_catalog.py#L1-L226) |
| **Evaluation** | EvalEngine | Deterministic + LLM-as-judge assessment | [biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py](/biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py#L1-L200) |
| **Evaluation** | AssertionChecker | Biomedical entity, safety, citation, regex checks | [biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py](/biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py#L62-L186) |
| **Schema** | io_types (Pydantic) | All inter-component data contracts | [biokernel/schema/io_types.py](/biokernel/schema/io_types.py#L1-L272) |

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L55-L199), [biokernel/adapters/factory.py](/biokernel/adapters/factory.py#L1-L119), [biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py](/biokernel/evaluator/eval_engine.py#L1-L200), [biokernel/schema/io_types.py](/biokernel/schema/io_types.py#L1-L272)

## Data Flow: Request Lifecycle

The diagram below traces a single `AgentRequest` through the complete execution path, showing the data transformations at each stage and the schema types that cross component boundaries.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Interface as CLI / REST / MCP
    participant BK as BioKernel
    participant Router as SkillRouter
    participant Factory as LLMFactory
    participant Adapter as Provider Adapter
    participant LLM as LLM API

    User->>Interface: "Analyze JAK2 V617F in MPN"
    Interface->>BK: AgentRequest(query, provider_preference)
    BK->>Router: route(query)
    Router->>Router: _tokenize → _tfidf_vector → _cosine_similarity
    Router-->>BK: [(skill_id, score), ...]
    BK->>BK: _build_system_prompt(skill_meta)
    BK->>Factory: create_provider("anthropic", config)
    Factory-->>BK: AnthropicAdapter (cached)
    BK->>Adapter: generate(LLMRequest)
    Adapter->>LLM: Claude API call
    LLM-->>Adapter: Raw response
    Adapter-->>BK: LLMResponse(text, usage, latency)
    BK->>BK: _check_safety(text)
    BK-->>Interface: AgentResponse(response, skill_used, safety_flags)
    Interface-->>User: Rendered result
```

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L231-L330), [biokernel/biokernel/router.py](/biokernel/biokernel/router.py#L68-L130), [biokernel/adapters/factory.py](/biokernel/adapters/factory.py#L68-L100)

## Skill Discovery and Registration

The platform employs a **dual-path discovery mechanism** that indexes skills at startup. The `_discover_skills` method scans all directories listed in `config.yaml`'s `skill_paths` (default: `Skills/`, `Skills/User_Collections/Babu/`, `skill collections/Antigravity_Skills/`). Two scanners operate in parallel:

- **SKILL.md Scanner**: Recursively finds `SKILL.md` files, parses their YAML frontmatter (using PyYAML for robust parsing), extracts name, description, tags, and capabilities from body headings, and registers them as `SkillType.SKILL_MD`. The full markdown body is stored as `instructions_body` for prompt construction.
- **Python Agent Scanner**: Discovers `*_agent.py` files, derives a hyphen-case `skill_id` from the relative path, and registers them as `SkillType.PYTHON_AGENT`.

The standalone `skills_catalog.py` module provides a complementary batch scanner that generates `skills_catalog.json` (a machine-readable index) and `skills_reliability_report.json` (source reliability scores). Both scanners validate required fields (`name`, `description`) and log warnings for malformed entries.

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L125-L230), [biokernel/skills_catalog.py](/biokernel/skills_catalog.py#L68-L175), [biokernel/config.yaml](/biokernel/config.yaml#L40-L44)

## Cross-Provider Abstraction: USDL and the Adapter Pattern

The platform's most architecturally significant contribution is the **USDL (Universal Skill Description Language)** transpilation layer. Rather than maintaining separate skill definitions per LLM provider, USDL defines a canonical `USDLSpec` — a dataclass containing name, description, inputs, outputs, safety checks, audit policy, and instructions body. The `USDLTranspiler` compiles this spec into three distinct output formats optimized for each provider's strengths:

| Provider | Prompt Format | Tool Schema | Special Features |
|----------|--------------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Anthropic** | XML-structured system prompt with `<instructions>`, `<safety>` blocks | Anthropic tool definitions (name + description + input_schema) | Thinking blocks, extended context |
| **OpenAI** | System message with markdown instructions | OpenAI function calling schemas (JSON Schema) | Structured JSON output, response format |
| **Gemini** | Role card with structured sections (Role, Objective, Instructions, Inputs) | Gemini-compatible function declarations | System instruction optimization |

The `LLMProvider` abstract base class enforces a uniform contract across all adapters: `initialize(config)`, `generate(request)`, `generate_with_tools(request, tool_executor)`, and `stream(request)`. The `LLMFactory` manages provider lifecycle with a class-level registry (supporting runtime plugin registration), instance caching, and a fallback chain that ensures graceful degradation when a preferred provider is unavailable.

> [!TIP]
> The USDL transpiler's `from_skill_md` classmethod automatically infers safety checks from body content — if the markdown body contains keywords like "safety", "risk", "contraindication", or "warning", it appends a safety review requirement without explicit configuration.

Sources: [biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py](/biokernel/optimizer/usdl_transpiler.py#L1-L200), [biokernel/interface/llm_provider.py](/biokernel/interface/llm_provider.py#L1-L121), [biokernel/adapters/factory.py](/biokernel/adapters/factory.py#L1-L119)

## Configuration and Runtime Behavior

Runtime behavior is governed by `config.yaml`, which defines provider models and API key environment variables, routing strategy and similarity thresholds, workflow engine parameters (DAG depth, step timeout, retry policy), and evaluation thresholds. The `load_config` function searches a precedence chain: explicit path → `BIOKERNEL_CONFIG` env var → `platform/config.yaml` → `config.yaml` → empty defaults.

| Configuration Domain | Key Parameters | Default |
|---------------------|----------------|---------|
| **Provider** | `default_provider`, per-provider `model`/`api_key_env`/`temperature` | `anthropic`, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, 0.3 |
| **Routing** | `strategy`, `similarity_threshold`, `fallback_skill` | `semantic`, 0.35, `general-biomedical-assistant` |
| **Workflow** | `max_dag_depth`, `step_timeout_seconds`, `retry_count`, `retry_delay_seconds` | 20, 120, 2, 5 |
| **System** | `log_level`, `max_concurrent_agents`, `enable_safety_checks` | INFO, 10, true |
| **Evaluation** | `pass_threshold`, `safety_pass_threshold` | 0.80, 0.95 |

Three execution modes are supported: **Autonomous** (automatic routing + execution for production APIs), **Interactive** (user selects from ranked skill matches for exploratory research), and **Manual** (user specifies exact `skill_id` for debugging and benchmarking). The `ExecutionMode` enum in the schema layer encodes these as `AUTONOMOUS`, `INTERACTIVE`, and `MANUAL`.

Sources: [biokernel/config.yaml](/biokernel/config.yaml#L1-L76), [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L40-L53), [biokernel/schema/io_types.py](/biokernel/schema/io_types.py#L30-L47)

## Interface Layer: REST, CLI, and MCP

The platform exposes three complementary interfaces, each suited to a different consumption pattern:

**REST API (FastAPI)**: Serves six endpoints on port 8000 — `GET /` (health), `POST /v1/agent/run` (single query execution), `POST /v1/workflow/run` (DAG workflow), `GET /v1/skills` (skill listing), `GET /v1/providers` (provider availability), and `POST /v1/route` (routing preview without execution). The application uses an async lifespan manager to initialize the BioKernel singleton at startup and tear it down on shutdown. CORS is configured with permissive defaults for development.

**CLI (`biokernel`)**: A click-based command with Rich terminal rendering. Commands include `serve` (start API server), `run` (execute query), `skills` (list skills with table output), `eval` (run evaluation suite with optional HTML report), `interactive` (REPL chat session), and `mcp` (start MCP server). The CLI gracefully degrades when Rich is unavailable, falling back to plain text output.

**MCP Server**: Implements the Model Context Protocol (spec 2024-11-05) over JSON-RPC 2.0 via stdio. Exposes four tools: `run_bio_agent` (execute skill), `list_skills` (discover skills), `route_query` (preview routing), and `run_workflow` (execute DAG). This enables seamless integration with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and any MCP-compatible client. Logging is redirected to stderr to avoid corrupting the JSON-RPC stdout channel.

Sources: [biokernel/biokernel/server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/server.py#L399-L547), [biokernel/cli.py](/biokernel/cli.py#L1-L200), [biokernel/biokernel/mcp_server.py](/biokernel/biokernel/mcp_server.py#L1-L200)
